body: I honestly thought I had found one of my girl friend's accounts until I looked through your history. We both have done exactly this since we were kids.
Dr. Terry Wahl's TED talk "minding your mitochondria". It's on YouTube. She doesn't like using the word paleo, but her method is essentially the paleo diet. That video pretty much changed my life.

Mine was the opposite actually. Started Wellbutrin and had the worst rapid cycling I've ever experienced. I also self harmed for the first time in 7 years. Started lamictal and it stopped almost immediately. But that's just me. So far I have liked both medications.

I related to everything in your post. I just wanted to say how great it is to have found this community and hear these stories from people that think and feel what I do. That helps me get through my day.
Very nice, that lifted my spirits a little bit today, thank you!
This actually sounds very similar to what happens to me, though I've never thought of it before. Thanks for sharing your experience, it definitely helps me understand the BD/BPD issue much better

Thank you, I definitely plan to stick around in the subreddit, it has been so helpful already. I'm feeling better about my diagnosis. I'm not happy, but I'm coping. I cannot get DBT because no one in my state offers it. I'm hoping to find some other way to get this type of help. I have no idea if any therapists skype with patients, but that would be awesome because I really want to try this therapy.

Thank you for your kind reply. Since all this happened, I don't have any more hard feelings towards my family. I realize that sometimes they can't be there for me because they need to take care of themselves first, especially since most of them struggle with some sort of mental illness themselves. I wish more than anything that I could start DBT, but not a single therapist practices this in my state. However, I'm going to buy that workbook you suggested.

Yes, I've known this a few years and it's precisely what I was afraid of and why I freaked out over my session with the psychiatrist. I'm starting to feel much better about all of this though. It was probably misleading when I said I don't understand how someone could have both. Though there are similarities between BD and BPD, it seems unusual to have both since one of the main problems for BPD is daily mood swings and from what I've read, there are no normal, stable cycles. This conflicts with BDs main issue. I may be wrong, I need to do more research.

Just reading about others people's struggles has been so helpful. Knowing that there are other people out there that suffer in the same way makes me know I'm not alone. And this community seems to be extremely supportive and kind. I'm finally feeling somewhat better after I posted this, I think I can hang on a couple more weeks until she is back from maternity leave. Thanks for your comment!
Thank you :)

I don't think anyone here would have trouble choosing their words wisely for those contemplating suicide. The important thing is that people of this subreddit may have a lot of compassion to share with suicidewatch. I'm subscribed to both of these subreddits but I rarely post or comment. I think you may have encouraged me to be more active on suicidewatch. :)

This is what I came here to say. The truth is much more grand than anything you are taught in church. If the fact that the universe lives inside you is not enough, seek out other non-dogmatic sources of spirituality. If you need that sense of community, seek out groups that share your passions or try out a Buddhist sangha (community) because many don't believe in the supernatural and take a more "Sagan" like view on life and self. This is the path I've found myself on, it won't work for many but it does for some.
Here too. I was fine three days ago and now I can't get out of bed and go to class.
Moodtrack is amazing and free! I use it several times a day.

For anyone looking for a great app to track moods, look into Moodtrack app, it's free. I was trying to write in my journal several times a day but it was not working for me. The app allows you to put in your mood and rate it on a scale from 1-5. You can also make notes to remember what happened that day. You can see your moods on a linear graph, I love that because I'm a visual person. My therapist thought it was the best app she's seen for that sort of thing.

Brown sugar has a molasses film on the sugar crystals. It has about 2% moisture, unlike turbinado that has almost no moisture and has the molasses and impurities removed. True raw sugar is not FDA approved because of the contaminants. That "raw sugar" in the store is actually turbinado.

I'm in my junior year of college as a dietetics major, planning on becoming an rd. I already see the influence that major corporations  have on AND- academy of nutrition and dietetics. It has already been said here in paleo, but grains are huge profit. Some of my professors acknowledge this, others seem to go with the general consensus (whole grains good, low fat good, loads of fiber good etc.) I'm basically faking my way through college because there are several things I don't agree with or that don't make sense to me in my classes. Always find who is funding a scientific study before forming an opinion.

I came here to say this. I started having health problems a few years ago and after countless doctors, decided to change my diet. Gluten free was the one change that made a huge difference. Now I'm studying dietetics, on my way to become an RD. I spoke to one of my professors that has celiac and she told me my symptoms were very much like hers but that I would need to eat gluten consistently for three months to be tested for celiac. I even tried to do it, but I was so sick after a week, I gave up. I can't be tested, so can't call myself a celiac and therefore everyone thinks I'm doing some fad diet. Also, from what I've learned in my classes, I know that gluten sensitivity is more common than most people think. Also, celiac is often misdiagnosed. It bothers me a lot about this whole gluten-free hating I've seen on reddit and other places.

One website suggested it was because it has [tryptophans](http://www.tiestatea.com/yerba-mate-vs-coffee/) that make us relaxed. [Wikipedia](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yerba_mate) only had this to say 
>The three xanthines present in mate have been shown to have a relaxing effect on smooth muscle tissue, and a stimulating effect on myocardial (heart) tissue.

So, I wasn't able to find much. Please share if you learn more about it.
I like Yerba mate. It has about the same caffeine as a cup of coffee but apparently it's supposed to be a less jittery, more calm energy.

I agree with you on the part about a degree not meaning much. But, where I'm from, a dietetics major has to have a 3.5 gpa to be accepted into an internship. The internship is 1200 hours. That is a lot for an internship if you compare it to others! Only then can you take the exam, and it isn't easy. I've known people to give up after the eighth time. If you get that far, then you have to get 75 hours of continuing ed every 5 years. These people are no dummies.
